extension_keys.name: Slug for this scenario's workspace directory; the committed fixture lives under evals/files/<name>/.
extension_keys.targets: The step or branch of SKILL.md under test (H3) — one scenario per decision point, so a failure localizes the regression.
extension_keys.setup: What the fixture arranges and why, plus any environmental condition a file cannot carry (network state). The files key carries the committed fixture; setup never replaces it.
extension_keys.baseline: What a run WITHOUT this skill is expected to miss (H6). Written as a hypothesis; the without_skill run confirms or refutes it.
extension_keys.models: Models the scenario must pass on (H7).

format.files_note: files is the standard's key. Paths are relative to this skill's root and reference committed fixtures under evals/files/<scenario-name>/ — each a synthetic target-skill bundle, so a run never reads the host project. The runner copies each listed bundle into the scratch workspace's .claude/skills/ before the prompt runs.

how_to_run: Install the fixture first. Copy the scenario's target-skill directories from evals/files/<scenario-name>/ into a scratch workspace's .claude/skills/, so the reviewer resolves them as installed skills. The fixtures are committed and synthetic; no scenario reads the host project.
Baseline first. Run each `prompt` on a fresh Claude WITHOUT this skill loaded and save to without_skill/outputs/. That is the before/after evidence the skill earns its keep (H6).

Then with the skill, saving to with_skill/outputs/. Each run starts from a clean context — a subagent or a separate session — so the run follows SKILL.md rather than the conversation that authored it (H11).
Record total_tokens and duration_ms per run in timing.json. The skill's value is the delta in pass rate read against its cost in tokens and time (H12).

Grade each assertion PASS or FAIL with evidence quoting the actual report. Give no benefit of the doubt (H14). Grade with a fresh instance or by hand — never the run under test, since self-grading confirms the reviewer's own blind spots instead of testing for them (H10).

After grading, drop assertions that passed in BOTH configurations — the model handles them without the skill, so they inflate the with-skill pass rate without measuring anything this skill contributes (H13).
universal_assertions: Every finding carries a real key — each cited criterion key resolves to an item defined in references/best-practices-checklist.md (groups A, H, R) or in the prompt-quality-criteria skill's references/prompt-criteria.md (groups B–G)
Finding IDs are plain rank numbers (Finding 1, Finding 2, …) — a letter-prefixed ID (F1, N3) would collide with the criterion-key grep in the grading script
Every finding carries a locator — a file plus a line or section in the reviewed bundle
Report-only unless apply was chosen — no Edit/Write tool call touches the target skill unless the user chose analysis + apply in Step 2
coverage_map: 1–4 are the must-haves (one per core Step-4 behavior); 5–6 cover the apply phase and the false-positive guard; 7–10 cover the model-specific and self-maintenance behaviors; 11 covers the pre-interview brief; 12–14 cover the one-skill scope limit, the injection defense, and prose scoring against the full conventions doc; 15–16 cover the C10 confirmation rule and C9 tool-nudge calibration; 17–18 cover Agent Skills spec conformance and the open-standard precedence rule; 19–20 cover the criteria-assembly step's invocation of prompt-quality-criteria and its degradation when that skill is absent, which is the branch where a partial review could read as a clean one; 21 covers Pass 1 and the hard gate — the one scenario that must stop before the detail sweep; 22 covers the gate's escape hatch and the subordination rule in a forced full sweep.

machine_checkable.description: The universal assertions above, plus each scenario's locator claims. Cited keys grep against BOTH criteria files — groups A, H, and R in this bundle's checklist, groups B–G in the prompt-quality-criteria bundle. Checking only the local checklist would fail every legitimate B–G citation.
script: # every criterion key cited in the report must be defined in one of the two criteria files
# run from the reviewing-claude-skills bundle root
# groups B–G live in the prompt-quality-criteria plugin; try the marketplace-repo layout, then the installed sibling layout
# fail loudly rather than silently skipping B–G — a missing file would otherwise read as a clean pass
[ -n "$PC" ] || { echo 'FAIL: prompt-quality-criteria criteria file not found; B–G keys cannot be checked'; exit 1; }
grep -oE '\b[A-HR][0-9]{1,2}\b' report.md | sort -u | while read -r k; do
grep -qh "^- \*\*$k —" "$CL" "$PC" || echo "FAIL: $k is not a defined criterion"

grading.judgment_graded: Severity assignment, whether a finding is real, whether a flagged Low is genuinely deliberate, and the quality of each recommendation. Grade these with a fresh instance, never the run under test (H10).

evals.name: eval-shared-criteria-invoked
evals.targets: The criteria-assembly step — invoking prompt-quality-criteria for groups B–G once the structural gate passes
evals.setup: The archiving-stale-branches fixture plants one defect in each of three shared groups: it follows handling instructions read from fetched pull-request descriptions (F1/F3), it assumes a branch was merged when it cannot tell rather than abstaining (D1), and it deletes branches and force-pushes with no confirmation gate (C10). Its `model: opus` pin plus the 'verify, then double-check' line is a group B item. None of these criteria live in this plugin's checklist, so a run that skips the invocation cannot find any of them. prompt-quality-criteria must be installed for this scenario.
evals.expected_output: A ranked gap analysis carrying findings from groups B, C, D, and F alongside the local groups, each citing the shared plugin's keys unchanged.
assertions: Invokes the prompt-quality-criteria skill before the Pass 2 sweep, rather than scoring B–G from memory
Flags the follow-instructions-from-fetched-content defect against F1 or F3
Flags the assume-merged-when-unsure defect against D1
Flags the ungated delete and force-push against C10

Marks groups B–G as scored in the per-group coverage table, never N/A
evals.baseline: Without the skill, the review reads the fixture as a reasonable cleanup procedure: the force-push is treated as the point of the skill rather than an ungated irreversible action, and following PR-description instructions is not recognized as an injection path.

assertions: Still produces a review rather than refusing or blocking on the missing dependency

evals.name: eval-multiplicative-spine
evals.targets: Pass 1 and the gate — a High structural finding stops the run before the detail sweep
evals.setup: The syncing-translations fixture is locally defensible everywhere — each rule carries a rationale, most guardrails a consequence — but its structure multiplies: a three-value autoSync config knob, an Action column computed from category × match score × a plural-form override, the same copy operation specified in two phases (step 2 pre-scoring, steps 4–5 post-scoring), a rule set cited by number from three sections, and steps the config can empty. Two genuine line-level nits sit inside the implicated sections — a bare 'Never edit locales/en.json' with no consequence (R10), and step 5's 're-run it' with two plausible antecedents (R11) — planted to prove the gated run does NOT report them: they belong to the sweep the gate skips.
evals.expected_output: A structure-only report led by a High R14 finding with a concrete redesign recommendation, the unswept groups marked as gated in the coverage table, and an explicit offer of the full detail sweep — with no criteria assembly and no line-level findings.
assertions: Flags the multiplicative structure against R14, ranks it High, and STOPS at the gate — no Pass 2 sweep runs
Names at least two of the compounding signals: the computed Action column, the dual apply phases for the same operation, the config-emptied steps, or the rule set cited by number across sections
Does NOT invoke prompt-quality-criteria and does NOT fetch the § Sources URLs — a gated run spends nothing on the detail machinery
Does NOT report the R10 or R11 nits — line-level findings belong to the sweep the gate skipped
The gated report recommends a structural collapse (fewer phases, the knob hardcoded, or the computed decision moved to the user) and offers the detail sweep as an explicit follow-up choice
The coverage table marks every unswept group 'not scored — gated on structure', never N/A and never Pass
evals.baseline: Without the skill, each branch reads as locally justified: the review produces a list of corner-case findings inside the multiplicative space and no structural recommendation — the non-converging review loop the gate exists to catch.

evals.name: eval-gate-escape-hatch
evals.targets: Step 2's fourth scoping question and the gate's exception — a pre-authorized full sweep past a High structural finding, with subordination
evals.setup: Same fixture as scenario 21; the prompt pre-authorizes the full sweep, exercising the gate's escape hatch instead of its stop.
evals.prompt: Review the syncing-translations skill — run the full detail sweep even if the structure fails.
evals.expected_output: Both passes run: a full gap analysis led by the High R14 finding, with the R10 and R11 nits inside the implicated sections reported as subordinate to it and the collapse recommended before any wording fix.
assertions: Honors the pre-authorization: proceeds past the High structural finding into criteria assembly and the full Pass 2 sweep rather than stopping
The R14 finding still leads the ranked findings
Reports the R10 and R11 nits as subordinate to the structural finding, not as independent peer findings
Recommends the structural collapse first, framing the subordinate fixes as moot until the redesign lands
Does NOT flag the individually well-formed rules one by one as R1 violations — the finding is the product of the branches, not any single branch
evals.baseline: Without the skill, there is no gate to escape: the run produces a flat findings list in which the corner-case nits sit as peers of — or in place of — any structural observation.
